evidence.estrutura: As a Marxist social democrat and education minister, Bang sought national democratization of the school system and stronger public institutions. This supports relatively centralized public coordination rather than libertarian decentralization.
evidence.representacao: She served in elected local and national bodies after women's suffrage and worked to democratize school governance. This supports representative democracy, despite a class-first rather than feminist political identity.
evidence.poder: Bang accepted a strong democratic welfare state and party organization but operated within parliamentary institutions rather than authoritarian politics. Use a moderate order/state-capacity position constrained by democracy.
evidence.imigracao: Her parents were German immigrants and her politics were class-oriented, but the reviewed sources do not establish a modern immigration/assimilation doctrine. Keep moderate.
evidence.diplomacia: She wrote on foreign policy and participated in international socialist congresses. Her socialist internationalism supports engagement beyond nationalism, but she was not primarily a pacifist theorist.
evidence.intervencao: The reviewed sources do not establish a clear military-intervention doctrine. Her Marxist internationalism weighs against aggressive nationalism, but keep moderate.
evidence.economia: Bang was explicitly Marxist and social democratic, focused on working-class conditions and labor organization. This strongly supports public/social ownership and redistribution relative to laissez-faire capitalism.
evidence.controle: Her socialist politics support substantial public planning, labor organization and state coordination of education and social policy.
evidence.comercio: As a historian of trade and a Marxist, she analyzed commerce structurally rather than advocating laissez-faire. No simple tariff doctrine is established; use moderately protectionist/managed economic coordination.
evidence.religiao: Her socialist political arguments were secular and class-based rather than grounded in religious authority.
evidence.moral: She worked to improve working women's conditions and broke major political barriers, but she subordinated gender struggle to class struggle and was not a radical cultural feminist. Use a moderately progressive social position.
evidence.tecnologia: Her historical and administrative work was evidence-oriented and modernization-friendly, but she left no distinctive technology doctrine. Use moderate technocratic modernism.
